desc: Verify whether the minimum weight path in G always has length at most 2 (diameter 2 in terms of minimum weight) by testing the counterexample with weights: assign small weights to k1 and k2 and large weights to other intervals to see if the left_min/right_min approach fails.

If diameter is not 2, design a segment tree / sweep line approach to compute left_min and right_min for paths of arbitrary length, or reduce the problem to a sparse graph (e.g., transitive reduction) for shortest path queries.
Implement the DSU-based connectivity algorithm for G by sweeping intervals and unioning with the rightmost disjoint interval to the left, to understand the component structure.
Investigate the transitive reduction of the interval order poset to see if it preserves the minimum weight path, and whether it has O(N) edges.
Consider reducing the problem to a shortest path problem on a graph with O(N) vertices and O(N log N) edges built from the segment tree, and apply Dijkstra or a custom algorithm for queries.
Once a correct algorithm is determined, implement and test it on the sample inputs, including the counterexample scenario.
